# nukadoko

Typed Gherkin / step contracts with tool-measured step records. Scenarios can fail statically before run; every run writes a Markdown run summary that a pull request carries. Declaration (contracts, `mutates`) is separate from observation (what the tool recorded).

It is not an untyped free-form agent runner, and it is not a substitute for human review: a person reads the `.feature` in the diff and the run summary, and approving the pull request is the sign-off.

Agent skills: [skills/acceptance/SKILL.md](skills/acceptance/SKILL.md), [skills/migration/SKILL.md](skills/migration/SKILL.md). Each entry says when to use it and which `references/` file beside it holds the procedure. `nuka skill path` prints the skills directory.

Installed package: `node_modules/nukadoko/skills/...` (this file at `node_modules/nukadoko/llms.txt`).

## Commands

The everyday loop is four things: a `.feature` file, a `defineStep` per kind of line, `nuka check`, and `nuka run`. README.md "Beside your unit tests" walks through it for a CLI project.

Everyday:

- `nuka init`: project setup with self-check; adds `.nukadoko/` to `.gitignore`, a `test:scenarios` script, the steps and the config to `tsconfig.json`'s `include`, and `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` to its `compilerOptions`
- `nuka scaffold <name> [--pattern <text>] [--then | --command [<entry point>]] [--from <step>.<key>] [--description <text>]`: a step stub that fails until implemented; `--description` writes the step's description, which is otherwise a TODO `nuka tend` reports as `step-description-todo`; `--from` writes the chain to an earlier step's returned value; `--command` writes a When step that runs a program and returns `exitCode`, `stdout`, and `stderr`; its value is the entry point, which must be an existing file that plain `node` can start (a `.ts` entry point importing an absent `./x.js` beside an `x.ts` is refused), and without one the step throws `fill in the entry point: <file>:<line>` until that line is filled in
- `nuka scaffold --feature <path>`: one stub for each line `nuka check <path>` calls `undefined-step`, the pattern read from the line (`{value:string}`, `{value:int}`, `{value:float}`) and `mutates: false` for a Then line; a line that reads more than one way, or whose reading would match another line, keeps its text as the pattern with no capture and gets a `note:` line on stderr
- `nuka check [feature..]`: static checks before run, for the files `nuka run` would select for the same targets (several files or a directory); the whole project with no target; a step that needs `playwright` the project has not installed is an error here
- `nuka run [feature..]`: execute scenarios, featuresDir with no target; first refuses what `check` refuses for its scenarios (`--no-check` skips that); records on stdout when it is not a terminal (`--records` writes them to a terminal too), progress and failures on stderr, a Markdown run summary (`--summary <path>` for a PR comment)
- `nuka steps` / `nuka describe <name>`: the vocabulary and one step's contract

Exploring:

- `nuka do <name>`: execute one typed step under its contract; step record on stdout
- `nuka session`: list, clear, start, or stop sessions
- `nuka harvest <step-record-ids..>`: draft a feature from `do` record ids
- `nuka explore <file> [--json]`: run a model or a relation against request-only steps; prints the shortest failing scenario, or one JSON object with `--json`

Upkeep:

- `nuka tend`: rot signals, never a gate by default
- `nuka clean`: delete accumulated records and cache under the state directory
- `nuka skill path`: where the bundled skills live

Experimental (may change without notice):

- `nuka experimental mcp-tools -- <command>`: list the tools another MCP server declares over stdio (not nukadoko's own vocabulary)
- `nuka experimental webmcp-tools <url>`: list the WebMCP tools a page declares

Prefer `check` before `run`. Do not treat agent narrative as the step record.
